question: According to the MUTCD, what exact percentage reduction in crashes is guaranteed by installing a STOP sign or all-way stop control?
model_answer: Direct Answer: The MUTCD does not state or guarantee any percentage reduction in crashes from installing a STOP sign or all-way stop control, and the evidence provided contains no such figure. Instead, the MUTCD uses crash history as a *warrant* (a threshold condition for considering installation), not as a promised safety outcome. The evidence is insufficient to cite any exact percentage, because none exists in these provisions. Guidance (recommended): - Minor-road stop control should be considered when, among other conditions, crash records show three or more reported crashes in a 12-month period (or six or more in 36 months for a four-leg intersection; five or more in 36 months for a three-leg intersection), where "The crashes should be susceptible to correction by installation of minor-road stop control" — this is a criterion for consideration, not a guaranteed reduction. Options (permitted): - All-way stop control may be installed where an engineering study indicates five or more reported crashes in 12 months (or six or more in 36 months) at a four-leg intersection, or four or more in 12 months (five or more in 36 months) at a three-leg intersection, of a type susceptible to correction by all-way stop control — again a warrant, not a performance guarantee. Citations: - Section 2B.11 Guidance §1 (p.78) - Section 2B.13 Option §1 (p.79)
